question:
The yellow light of a sodium lamp has an average wavelength of 5890 \AA. Calculate the energy in (a) electron volts and (b) kilocalories per mole.
Is the correct answer "(a) 2.8eV and (b) 64.7 Kcal/mole"?

claims.text: The proposed answer (2.8 eV and 64.7 kcal/mol) is incorrect in both parts.
Photon energy is given by E = hc/λ with hc ≈ 1239.8 eV·nm.
The energy of the 5890 Å photon is about 2.10 eV.
The proposed 64.7 kcal/mol is wrong, and the error carries over from part (a), since 64.7 corresponds to about 2.8 eV.
The physics is unambiguous and the calculation is direct.
A different value of hc or of the eV-to-kcal/mol factor could change the answer, but not enough to explain a discrepancy this large.
